name: Kyle's Motorcycle — Unbranded Matte-Black Standard
description:
A matte-black standard-class motorcycle of indeterminate manufacture, the kind of bike that gets built in a back-shop garage from parts that came off seven different production frames. No corponation branding anywhere on it. No registration plate visible from the road; the plate is there, magnetized to the underside of the rear cowl, and Kyle moves it around depending on which Tier the contract is in. The bike is fast enough, light enough, and forgettable enough — the three qualities Kyle wants in transportation he might have to leave somewhere and walk away from.

Kyle parks it at ground level. He could pay for vertical garage space (most West Town buildings have at least token bike-rack hooks at the second-story setback), but ground level is where everyone else parks, and Kyle is not in the business of advertising that he has more options than the people whose work he competes for. The bike sits outside The Pivot most nights, against the alley wall, under whatever overhang catches the worst of the rain. Sometimes it sits at Mrs. Chen's noodle stall. Sometimes at the trailhead of the Gray Zone eastern strut, two blocks south of the loading dock that will not have a happy night.

The bike is unobtrusive in a city where the rich travel by VTOL and the corponations travel by armored convoy. It is part of how Kyle keeps the surface of his life looking like he belongs to the same Tier his contracts are written from.
manufacturer: Custom — back-shop assembly from mixed production parts
tier_availability: Tier 2 / Tier 3 — the bike type is common in the GLMZ ground-level transit economy. Kyle's specific build is one of a kind by accumulation.
legality: Legal, technically. Plate is current. Registration is in the name of a person who exists on paper but does not, strictly speaking, exist in the flesh — one of Sable's discreet legal-fiction services.
specifications: class: standard / naked | drivetrain: electric, single motor, mid-mounted | range: ~300 km nominal, ~220 km in continuous GLMZ rain | top speed: irrelevant — Kyle does not need the top speed and does not chase the kind of trouble that requires it | weight: ~190 kg dry | finish: matte black throughout, deliberately unbranded | storage: small underseat compartment, magnetic plate-mount under rear cowl, a removable saddle bag Kyle uses to carry the moon clips for Chorus when he is expecting to fire it
tactical_use: Distance. Kyle uses the bike to cover ground inside GLMZ and occasionally outside it — Pulse stations across the GLMZ are reachable by surface routes that move on the bike's schedule rather than the corponation transit schedule. He does not ride into firefights. He rides to a block from one and walks the rest. The bike's job is to be where he left it when he comes back.
cultural_context: Ground-tier travel in GLMZ is a statement of where you live and how much margin you have. Walking is what the lowest tier does. VTOL is what the highest tier does. The middle — Kyle's working tier — moves on bikes, on the surface rail, on the converted electrics that used to be delivery scooters. Kyle's specific bike, the unbranded matte-black build, is doing exactly what it looks like it's doing: not making any claims. Laugh or you'd cry: in a city where every other vehicle is leasing its livery space, Kyle's bike has no name and that is the loudest thing about it.
story_hooks: Someone tries to steal the bike from outside The Pivot. The plate they read is current. The plate they read is also magnetically attached and the bike's actual ID is in the wheel hub controller, which is locked to Kyle's NeoCortex signature. The would-be thief gets the bike moving roughly ten meters before the controller decides he is not Kyle and the bike stops, hard, in the alley. He limps away. The bike is where Kyle left it when he comes back.

Kyle parks the bike at the trailhead of a contract that goes worse than expected. He walks back to it hours later, bleeding, missing pieces he started the day with. The bike is exactly where he left it. So is the moon-clip bag in the saddle compartment, which he forgot to bring with him. He notes the lesson.

physical_description.visual_profile: Matte black throughout. No livery. No fairing decals. The kind of bike that reads as 'someone's daily ride' rather than 'someone's statement.' Standard riding position, no cafe-racer crouch, no aggressive forward lean. Practical.
physical_description.dimensions: Standard-class envelope. Approximately 2.1 m long. Approximately 110 kg dry mass.
physical_description.weight_description: ~190 kg dry. Light enough to muscle out of a tight parking situation without help. Heavy enough that the steering feels stable in GLMZ wind.
physical_description.primary_material: Steel frame, composite bodywork, standard electric drivetrain.
physical_description.color_scheme: Black. Plus whatever the alley wall is reflecting on a given night.
distinctive_features: No corponation branding anywhere — frame, fairing, wheels, controller all unmarked
Magnetic plate-mount under the rear cowl — Kyle changes plates by Tier
Underseat compartment Kyle uses to carry Chorus moon clips when expecting a fight
Single saddle bag — usually empty, usually unzipped, usually wet
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained. Kyle does the maintenance himself. Cables tight, brakes recently bled, tires within wear limit. The kind of vehicle that gets ridden, not garaged.
